points.why: Frames the test around whether plausible input values push the 18% below the 10% target, which is the decision margin.
Describes one-at-a-time swings across ranges with the others held at best guess, shown as a tornado chart, framed against the 10% threshold.
Notes that one-at-a-time swings miss interactions and proposes joint Monte Carlo sampling with variance attribution, a global method in substance, though it doesn't name Morris or Sobol.
Concludes with a ranked shortlist of 2–4 inputs for a targeted study instead of blanket collection or a bare robustness claim.
